keypoints_from_image2d — REPRCONV keypoint op

• Data kinds: image2d → keypoints

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.keypoints_from_image2d(image2d, threshold=0.0) (to call the implementation directly, import reprconv; reprconv.keypoints_from_image2d(image2d, threshold=0.0); from the registry, opsreprconv.get("keypoints_from_image2d"))

Usage

A count/response image (H, W) → image coordinates (N,2) = (u, v). The way back of the round trip.

Splits the pixels > threshold into connected components with 8-neighbourhood and returns the intensity-weighted centroid of each component. It is weighted so that for response images that still hold subpixel information (correlation peaks etc.) the round-trip error can be brought below quantisation.

Note that the 8-neighbourhood connectivity is the main culprit of loss: 2 points that land on adjacent pixels fuse into 1 component, and the centroid moves to the midpoint of the 2 points. selftest measures "quantisation error of well-separated points only" and "overall including fusion" separately (mixing them would make comparison with the theoretical quantisation value 0.2887 px impossible).

Args:

image2d: (H, W) real image.

threshold: only pixels exceeding this value are picked up.

Returns:

(N, 2) float64 (u, v). Row order is the label order of scipy.ndimage.label.

Raises:

ValueError: not 2-D / non-finite / not even 1 pixel exceeds the threshold.
